nodes.title: Morita degrees
nodes.statement: At a place i of residue degree d_i let δ_i(x)=deg(H_{i,a_i}) for the Morita component of the distinguished isotropic Iwahori subgroup, with valuation v_p(p)=1. It lies in [0,d_i a_i]. In type A use one member of the polarization-paired factors. Degrees are invariant under extension of complete valued fields and additive in exact sequences of finite flat groups.

Fix a sufficiently large p-adic coefficient field, neat tame level, compatible toroidal fans, a polarization convention and totally positive elements x_i with valuation one at the selected p-adic place and zero at the others. Type-A signatures (a_i,b_i) are constant at embeddings over a place.

Apply additivity before restoring the residue-degree factor; retain the integral model in the valuation domains.

nodes.statement: There is C(p), independent of tame level, such that for k≥C(p),r≥p²+p the operator T₁ is zero on the rank-zero stratum modulo p. Together with Hasse-invariant commutations this yields nilpotence of the appropriate powers on its thickenings.
hypotheses: Use the genus-two Siegel variety over Q with neat tame level prime to p, its compatible toroidal/minimal compactifications and boundary D. The coefficient sheaf is Ω(k,r)=Sym^k(ω)⊗det(ω)^r, with k≥0; each result specifies the extra bound on r.

The singular Klingen Iwasawa complex and its one-variable character convention are imported from HigherHidaAndColemanTheory:X8/klingen-complex and klingen-control. The affinoid-height-one Igusa maps are affine étale, not asserted finite.
proofSteps: On p-rank zero every rank-p³ subgroup contains the Frobenius kernel.
Factor the isogeny through Frobenius to obtain the extra coefficient divisibility.
Apply Artin–Rees to the fundamental-class lattice and a finite cover to make C independent of tame level.

acceptance: The nilpotence bound is independent of tame level, and passage to a thickening retains a quantitative power rather than asserting immediate vanishing there.

For k≥C(p),r≥2 its ordinary part e(T)RΓ(X₁^{≥1},Ω(k,r)(−D)) is a perfect F_p-complex of amplitude [0,1]. The restriction from the global spherical X₁ ordinary complex is a quasi-isomorphism when r≥3; at r=2 it is an isomorphism on H⁰ and injective on H¹. Thus the same global amplitude follows here only for r≥3. No integral global amplitude is inferred from this special-fiber theorem.

nodes.title: Torsion continuation and tube comparison
nodes.statement: For k,r≥0, 0≤ε<1 and a nonzero finite U-slope block whose roots all have valuation <b(k,r), global cohomology maps quasi-isomorphically to the height-one tube cohomology. The statement holds for canonical and subcanonical coefficients. Intersecting with the BGG ranges gives all-degree algebraic comparison for s<min(b,k−2), and H⁰-isomorphism/H¹-injectivity for s<min(b,k+1).

proofSteps: Choose ε′>0 small enough that b−2ε′(k+r)−s>0 for every root in the finite block.
Extend modulo precision growing linearly with the number of bad iterates; lose only a fixed constant on compatibility.
For P(X) annihilating a finite block with P(0)≠0, set Q(X)=−(P(X)−P(0))/(XP(0)); this is a polynomial and UQ(U)=1 on the block. Apply this inverse polynomial at every extension step.

gaps.title: Scope of the signed PEL estimate
gaps.detail: The BPS degree lower bound cannot be multiplied by a negative terminal weight without reversing its direction. This plan proves the stated positive-terminal-weight region with nonnegative eigenvalue slopes; extending to the paper’s unrestricted signed-weight formulation needs a separate estimate.

gaps.title: Dimension-one PEL reduction
gaps.detail: The original source invokes modular-curve continuation in dimension one. A classification/reduction covering every possible dimension-one PEL factor has not been supplied; the new theorem is restricted to components of dimension>1.

gaps.title: Finite-block topology in torsion comparison
gaps.detail: The source’s bounded-cocycle argument must be strengthened by continuity and boundedness of the finite-slope projection on cohomology modulo boundaries. The target records this proof obligation; bounded cocycles alone do not prove the required bounded classes.

gaps.title: Euler characteristic versus torsion
gaps.detail: Pilloni Remark 1.4 and Remark 15.2.1 formulate stronger torsion/support-dimension predictions. No torsion theorem is inferred from virtual rank zero; packet-balance and local-level comparison remain explicit supplier contracts.

gaps.title: Integral Hilbert descent with p-torsion deck quotient
gaps.detail: The direct-factor descent used in BCGP21 Proposition 4.4.3 needs derived invariants if the deck/unit quotient has p-torsion. Neatness does not imply p∤|Δ|. The integral common-similitude theorem here imposes p∤|Δ|; extending to all levels requires a separate descent argument.

gaps.title: Multivariable Hasse powers
gaps.detail: The simultaneous-powers exact sequence invoked in Proposition 4.6.19 fails for two independent parameters. The corrected single-exponent induction needs the precise regular-sequence and supported-acyclicity input requested from C5; until supplied, this control proof is not closed.

gaps.title: Finite-block completion and analytic intersections
gaps.detail: The exact continuous finite-block projection on the completed Čech complex, and acyclicity of every cube intersection for the analytic coefficient, are needed for injectivity and amplitude. Neither follows merely from projectivity of charts. Supplier statements and proof obligations are explicit.

gaps.title: Strength of Hilbert rational comparison
gaps.detail: The two-term Euler argument applies to |I|=1 after non-Eisenstein localization and individual-operator integrality. A full classical comparison for arbitrary |I| or an integral comparison without the stated deck condition is not a consequence of these sources.

gaps.title: Completed analytic localization carrier
gaps.detail: The current algebraic highest-weight roadmap does not supply the canonical completion, continuous dual, λ-action twist and analytic localization of O(𝔤,𝔟)_{λ-alg}. gaps.title: Exact eigenpacket and packet balance
gaps.detail: Taking m-annihilated eigenspaces is not exact. BCGP25 Theorem 4.12.4(3) assumes four equal graded eigenspace dimensions independently of the image hypotheses; Lemma 4.12.3 proves only total tensor multiplicity. The corrected classicality target retains that balance as a hypothesis. Applying it requires a separate verification, such as the multiplicity-one bounds in Remark 4.12.5, as well as the stable classical automorphic-packet comparison.

gaps.title: Full-torus and tame descent refinement
gaps.detail: The projectivity argument needs the cofinal full-torus integral control and tame-boundary stabilizer calculation, including p=2 and p-divisible Δ. These are requested explicitly; semisimple finite-character splitting or averaging would not close this stage.

gaps.title: Singular localization overlap kernel
gaps.detail: BCGP25 Proposition 3.6.15 uses injectivity of (x+1)∂_x+1 at an overlap fiber. The germ 1/(1+x) is an ambient kernel element. Its membership in the constrained fiber is not established, so this is a proof gap rather than a counterexample to the proposition. Supply the missing fiber restriction or a different nonzero intertwiner before closing the Sen–Cousin theorem or its classicality application. This independently reproduces the reviewed extraction finding PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-PILLONI-25/E015.
